name: Unrest
label: Simple Machines
lede: A teenager's label, a band that refused to repeat a song, and a run of records that went from cassette noise to 4AD pop in under a decade.

eras.title: A teenager's label, a band that never repeats itself
eras.text: Mark Robinson starts Teenbeat Records while still in high school and Unrest as its house band. Early on the rule is never to play the same song twice, and the records swing between punk, funk and noise.

years.cap: Mark Robinson and Phil Krauth in the early days
years.h: Teenbeat starts as a high-schooler's label; Unrest is its band
years.p: [[Mark Robinson|fc1a1e50-b6f7-431f-834b-d1441e54dcb7]] founds Teenbeat Records while still in high school, and the self-titled Unrest cassette appears May 1, 1985.
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes the early Unrest as an experimental project built on never playing the same song twice, drawing on punk, funk and Ennio Morricone. Robinson and drummer Phil Krauth were the core.

The cassette was among the first releases on what became one of the most durable one-person indie labels in Washington.

years.h: Malcolm X Park arrives on Teenbeat and Caroline
years.p: Named for a D.C. park, the LP is Unrest's first record with Caroline distribution behind it.

eras.title: Bridget Cross plugs in the bass
eras.text: Bridget Cross joins on bass and the band turns toward lively, minimalist pop, while still leaving room for white noise, sirens and beeps between the songs.

years.h: Bridget Cross joins on bass
years.p: [[Bridget Cross|11a8f5ae-5a31-4258-8c4d-87ea4c44c197]] arrives in 1990, and Wikipedia credits her with steering Unrest toward a "minimalist but lively kind of pop".

years.h: Kustom Karnal Blackxploitation lands on Teenbeat/Caroline
years.p: Pop songs sit beside avant-garde percussion and noise tracks, the mix that becomes Unrest's signature.

years.h: Split 7-inch with Shudder to Think
years.p: Unrest shares a 1990 split single with fellow D.C. band [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]], part of a run of 7-inches Robinson issues on Teenbeat.

years.h: Recording Imperial f.f.r.r. at Fun City in New York
years.p: Unrest spends July 15 to 27 at the Fun City studio in New York with engineer [[Wharton Tiers|de3636ee-5022-462b-b427-34be9674f281]], and Krauth and Robinson co-produce.

years.h: A track on Simple Machines' Fortune Cookie Prize compilation
years.p: Simple Machines, the Arlington label run out of a house, includes Unrest on its Fortune Cookie Prize comp, the start of the band's link to the Simple Machines scene.
years.xp: Simple Machines also put out the Inclined Plane singles series (with [[Tsunami|fea43e99-c4d5-4dac-9c27-868e864c6dc2]], [[Superchunk|61653550-fd9b-4401-8248-44f2d064d384]], [[Rodan|1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd]] and Unrest) and the Machines 1990–1993 compilation, per the label's discography on Wikipedia.

eras.title: The big two: Imperial and Perfect Teeth
eras.text: Unrest makes the records that define it: Imperial f.f.r.r. gets it named a top album of the year by Spin, and 4AD picks the band up for Perfect Teeth. The EPs in between are as good as the albums.

years.h: Imperial f.f.r.r. puts Unrest on the map
years.p: Released through No.6 and Teenbeat, it ranks 8th on Spin's 1992 albums of the year and later lands on Alternative Press's 90 greatest albums of the 90s.
years.xp: The UK edition on Guernica added four bonus tracks. A 2005 remaster added nine more, alternate versions and unreleased material, and a vinyl reissue followed in 2009.

years.h: Isabel Bishop EP, Unrest's first for 4AD
years.p: Teenbeat and 4AD release the EP, named for the American painter, as Ivo Watts-Russell's label starts working with the band.

years.h: Five days at Pachyderm with Brian Paulson
years.p: Unrest records Perfect Teeth at Pachyderm Studio in Minnesota with producer [[Brian Paulson|65f13d3b-ddd6-4b33-8ab7-366ee7fb63c4]], who had worked on Slint's Spiderland. The band cuts about 20 songs and picks 11.

years.h: Cath Carroll EP on Teenbeat and 4AD
years.p: Another EP named for a person, released a few weeks before the album.

years.h: Perfect Teeth: a 7-inch box set from 4AD
years.p: The album first appears as a box of 7-inch singles, and Wikipedia calls it the band's best seller at about 15,000 copies by SoundScan.
years.xp:
Simon Le Bon of Duran Duran is credited as producer. Per Wikipedia, the band made the joke credit and the label took it seriously, so Le Bon visited the studio for two days without producing anything.

AllMusic's Heather Phares gave the album 4.5 stars and called it the band's peak.

years.h: Live in Newcastle, opening for Stereolab
years.p: On tour in Britain, Unrest plays Newcastle on August 4, 1993, a show Teenbeat later released as a live album (2009).
years.xp: Unrest also shared a 1993 split 7-inch with [[Stereolab|f1df0431-9250-4ec8-95d8-f19ce7cf7fb6]] and supported them on tour after Perfect Teeth.

eras.title: The end, and Air Miami
eras.text: Unrest dissolves in 1994. Robinson had reportedly drafted a follow-up called Air Jamaica, but instead he and Bridget Cross start Air Miami.

years.big: Next up was going to be Air Jamaica
years.h: Unrest ends, with a follow-up album already sketched
years.p: Unrest breaks up after Perfect Teeth, with Mark Robinson saying he had cover designs ready for a next album titled Air Jamaica.
years.xp:
Robinson told It's Psychedelic Baby that the band did not know Perfect Teeth would be its last, and that he had already drafted plans and preliminary artwork for Air Jamaica.

Robinson and Cross went on to form [[Air Miami|fdc1eb7c-3ad2-4c4a-abf7-81b42f56b989]] with Mike Fellows and Lauren Feldsher.

years.h: Air Miami: Robinson and Cross start over
years.p: [[Air Miami|fdc1eb7c-3ad2-4c4a-abf7-81b42f56b989]] releases the Airplane Rider single in 1994 and the Me. Me. Me. LP on 4AD and Teenbeat in 1995; it ends in 1996.

eras.title: Reunions and reissues
eras.text: Unrest plays a one-off reunion in 2005, tours the East Coast in 2010, and its catalog gets remastered and reissued. Teenbeat keeps the archive open.

years.h: Reunion at the Black Cat for Teenbeat's 20th
years.p: Unrest plays Washington's Black Cat on February 24, 2005, on a bill with Eggs, +/-, True Love Always and others. Teenbeat later issued the show as a live album (2009).

years.h: Imperial f.f.r.r. gets a remastered edition
years.p: A 2005 remaster adds nine bonus tracks of alternate versions and unreleased material.

years.h: Bridget Cross records as Maybe It's Reno
years.p: Her self-titled Teenbeat album has Mark Robinson and Phil Krauth on its first seven tracks.

years.h: A short East Coast reunion tour
years.p: Unrest gets back together for a small run of East Coast dates in July 2010.

years.h: Perfect Teeth back as a colored-vinyl box
years.p: Teenbeat reissues the album with a 24-page booklet of Robinson's photographs.

years.h: Perfect Teeth gets an expanded 30th-anniversary edition
years.p: Remastered, with new art by Chris Bigg, a 16-page zine with liner notes from the band and 4AD founder Ivo Watts-Russell, and a companion album, Extra Teeth, of B-sides and rarities.

sources.title: It's Psychedelic Baby: Perfect Teeth Turns 30
